related_questions.question: What is the gestational diabetes mellitus?
related_questions.snippet: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a form of hyperglycemia that develops during pregnancy and poses risks to both mother and fetus. The diagnostic criteria for GDM have evolved over decades, reflecting advancements in glucose testing methods and a deeper understanding of associated risks.
related_questions.title: Gestational Diabetes - StatPearls - NCBI Bookshelf

related_questions.question: Is gestational diabetes mellitus a serious problem?
related_questions.snippet: Gestational diabetes raises the risk of high blood pressure. It also raises the risk of a serious complication of pregnancy that causes high blood pressure and other symptoms, called preeclampsia. These conditions can threaten your life and your baby's life.
related_questions.title: Gestational diabetes - Symptoms & causes - Mayo Clinic

related_questions.question: Is diabetes mellitus the same as gestational diabetes?

text_blocks.snippet: No, diabetes mellitus and gestational diabetes are not the same, though they are related. Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a broader term encompassing various conditions where the body doesn't properly use or produce insulin, leading to high blood sugar. Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a specific type of diabetes that develops during pregnancy in women who did not previously have diabetes.
snippet_highlighted_words: No, diabetes mellitus and gestational diabetes are not the same, though they are related

list.title: Onset:
list.snippet: GDM develops during pregnancy, while DM can exist before pregnancy (Type 1 and Type 2) or develop during pregnancy (GDM).

list.title: Cause:
list.snippet: DM can be caused by the body's inability to produce insulin (Type 1) or by insulin resistance (Type 2). GDM is often caused by hormones produced during pregnancy that interfere with insulin's ability to regulate blood sugar, leading to insulin resistance.

list.title: Duration:
list.snippet: GDM usually resolves after delivery, while DM can be a lifelong condition.

list.title: Risk:
list.snippet: Women with GDM have a higher risk of developing Type 2 diabetes later in life, according to the American Diabetes Association.
Both involve high blood sugar levels.
Both can be managed with diet, exercise, and medication if necessary.
Both can have potential health consequences for the mother and baby if not managed effectively.

text_blocks.snippet: In essence, GDM is a temporary condition that can arise during pregnancy, while DM is a broader disease with different forms and potential long-term implications, according to the American Diabetes Association.

related_questions.question: What is the main cause of gestational diabetes?
related_questions.snippet: Pregnant women who can't make enough insulin during late pregnancy develop gestational diabetes. Being overweight or having obesity is linked to gestational diabetes. Women who are overweight or have obesity may already have insulin resistance when they become pregnant.
related_questions.title: Symptoms & Causes of Gestational Diabetes - NIDDK

text_blocks.snippet: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a condition where high blood sugar develops during pregnancy in women who did not have diabetes before becoming pregnant. It typically develops in the second or third trimester and often resolves after childbirth. While it can cause complications during pregnancy and delivery, it is manageable with proper care.
snippet_highlighted_words: a condition where high blood sugar develops during pregnancy in women who did not have diabetes before becoming pregnant

list.title: Definition:
list.snippet: GDM is characterized by high blood sugar levels during pregnancy, even if the woman was not previously diabetic.

list.title: Timing:
list.snippet: It usually appears in the second or third trimester, between the 24th and 28th weeks of pregnancy, but can occur earlier.

list.title: Prevalence:
list.snippet: GDM affects a significant number of pregnancies, with estimates ranging from 5% to 9% of US pregnancies, according to the CDC.

list.title: Risk Factors:
list.snippet: Overweight or obese women, those with a family history of diabetes, and certain ethnic groups (like Asians, American Indians, Indigenous Australians, and Pacific Islanders) are at higher risk.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: Some women may experience increased thirst, frequent urination, or fatigue, but many have no noticeable symptoms.

list.title: Complications:
list.snippet: GDM can lead to complications like preeclampsia (high blood pressure during pregnancy), macrosomia (excessively large baby), and increased risk of cesarean delivery.

list.title: Management:
list.snippet: GDM is often managed through diet and exercise, and sometimes medication (insulin or oral medications).

list.title: Long-term Implications:
list.snippet: Women with GDM have an increased risk of developing type 2 diabetes later in life.

list.title: Resolution:
list.snippet: In most cases, GDM resolves after delivery, but it's crucial to manage blood sugar levels during pregnancy to minimize risks to both mother and baby.
